Native reporting, audit and explicit optional Python bridge exports

etr_native_release_source_bridge_reporting.Rd

Reference index for exported functions in this scientific domain. The functions are independently callable; scientific scope and input contracts vary by estimator, data structure, fitted object, and selected backend.

Details

Bridge functions may require a separate compatible Python installation; they explicitly expose third-party scikit-fda or FDApy objects and MUST NOT be described as Python-free numerical native R implementations. Portable writer and reporting functions serialize or describe provenance, schema fields, execution steps and scientific decisions, which do not by themselves prove source parity. The source-contract review queue is an unsigned author-side review artifact; it does not approve scientific contracts. All external approvals require genuine independent review.

Optional Python FData source-constructor geometry in native R

The opt-in etr_to_skfda_grid(trajectories, strict_source_record=TRUE) returns a typed R record of the frozen Python 1.2 scikit-fda constructor arguments: unmodified curve-by-time-by-coordinate values, source time grid, dataset name and coordinate names. It retains the one-domain normalized grid and zero-based source curve positions for scientific inspection. It does not return a real Python skfda.FDataGrid instance.

The opt-in etr_to_fdapy_irregular(trajectories, dimension, strict_source_record=TRUE) returns separate irregular input_dim_0 sample-time arrays and observed selected-channel value arrays under the source zero-based observation keys. Source mode accepts legitimate two-visit irregular curves and requires finite selected values; all other channels remain unaltered. It does not return a real Python FDApy.IrregularFunctionalData instance. The original native fdapace adapter is the default, with its distinct minimum-observation restrictions.

Both opt-in modes preserve observations without interpolation, imputation or fitting. Frozen Python source-constructor equivalence is limited to these scientific arrays and labels. The actual scikit-fda/FDApy backend class methods, projected bases, PACE estimators and Python exception objects remain separately unqualified. Independent full-contract source certification is pending. See docs/native-skfda-fdapy-source-constructor-records-20261112.md.

Exported entry points

etr_detect_functional_outliers_skfda

detect functional outliers skfda – an explicit exported method; consult its R formal arguments and source-contract restrictions.

etr_export_python_portable_result

Writes common-grid and irregular trajectories, dense FPCA and MFPCA fits, and compositional FPCA fits in the Python 1.2 JSON and NPZ snapshot format. Irregular samples keep their curve-specific grids and matrix shapes. Metadata columns are ordered and indexed by curve ID, with numeric, character and logical vectors supported. Missing character and logical cells are JSON nulls. The dense fit carries the R component count, scaling and total variance under provenance$native_r_fpca. Its Python model field is null. Compositional fits retain their zero-based reference dimension, epsilon and nested dense fit. Exports record the R package version. Both overwrite and include_environment must be false, and the destination must be new or empty.

Source-sampled scikit-fda basis projection

An additional opt-in etr_to_skfda_basis(trajectories, dimension, basis="bspline", n_basis=15L, order=4L, strict_source_record=TRUE) computes the frozen Python 1.2 scikit-fda sampled least-squares scientific coefficients on the original complete observed time grid. The native R QR solver is used on the actual source-compatible B-spline or Fourier basis values without interpolation or regularization.

The Fourier mode uses the normalized 1/sqrt(T), sqrt(2/T) sin(2*pi*k*t/T) and sqrt(2/T) cos(2*pi*k*t/T) columns, and automatically expands even requested basis counts to the next odd count, preserving the originally requested count separately in the frozen-source scientific result fields. B-spline mode retains the source uniformly placed interior knots and endpoint repetition. Strict numerical mode requires a finite complete grid and full-column-rank basis design; the broader singular and underdetermined Python backend domain remains outside the reviewed scientific contract.

The return is a typed native R scientific basis record with an explicit backend_object=NULL; it is not a real Python skfda.FDataBasis instance. The legacy native R basis projection remains the default and unchanged. Independent Python object identity and whole-domain backend equivalence are not certified. See docs/native-skfda-basis-sampled-ls-source-20261112.md.

Modified Band Depth source-scientific functional boxplot

The opt-in etr_detect_functional_outliers_skfda(trajectories, dimension, method="boxplot", factor=1.5, random_state=0L, strict_source_record=TRUE) implements the frozen Python 1.2 scikit-fda BoxplotOutlierDetector's deterministic default method through a native R ModifiedBandDepth functional data record.

Each selected observed channel curve receives pointwise SimplicialDepth based on all distinct pairs of training curves. The depth profile is integrated using SciPy-compatible composite Simpson quadrature on the actual (possibly nonuniform) observed time grid. The deepest ceil(n/2) curves define the functional central region, which is expanded by factor times the pointwise central-envelope width. A curve is flagged for scientific review if any point lies outside this functional fence.

Strict source mode is bounded to complete finite input and untied deepest-half cutoff depths. It returns native R labels, modified-band depths, Simpson weights and central/non-outlying envelope diagnostics, never a real Python scikit-fda detector. The stochastic method="msplot" requires different directional-outlyingness and robust MCD calculations and is explicitly not supported by this scientific review. The historical marginal pointwise Tukey alternative remains the default when strict_source_record=FALSE. Full Python class/exception and MSPlot-method contract equivalence is not claimed. See docs/native-skfda-mbd-functional-boxplot-source-20261112.md.

Fixed-spectrum FDApy PACE numerical source stage

Opt-in etr_fit_sparse_fpca_fdapy(trajectories, dimension, n_components, strict_source_record=TRUE, source_fit_snapshot=...) evaluates the native R numerical FDApy 1.0.x UFPCA conditional PACE score stage, provided a genuine already fitted FDApy source eigensystem and source-centered irregular observations in source_fit_snapshot.

The supplied snapshot must contain mean_grid, eigenfunctions, eigenvalues, noise_variance and a centered_observations list, all in original curve order and with eigenfunctions on the exact sorted pooled observation times. The native score estimator follows source FDApy's actual internal np.interp pooled-grid interpolation, including constant endpoint extension, spectral covariance reconstruction and pseudoinverse (t(Phi) diag(lambda) Phi + max(tol, noise_variance)*I)^+; the scores are reconstructed with the supplied eigenfunctions and mean.

This stage does NOT fit FDApy's penalized B-spline or local-polynomial mean/covariance smoothers or estimate its eigenpairs. normalize=TRUE and the source backend Python UFPCA object and classes are NOT implemented. Its semantic coverage is specifically restricted to fixed-source-spectrum PACE scoring and inverse reconstruction; the native full sparse-FPCA model-fitting source gap remains open in inst/extdata/native_scoped_fdapy_submethod_gaps_20261112.csv. Historical backend="fdapace" remains unchanged by default. See docs/native-fdapy-fixed-spectrum-pace-20261112.md.

FDApy 1.0.x native raw-data PS/LP covariance UFPCA fit

The opt-in etr_fit_sparse_fpca_fdapy(trajectories, dimension, n_components, strict_source_record=TRUE, source_fit_snapshot=NULL, fit_smoothing="PS", score_smoothing="LP", tol=1e-4, normalize=FALSE, kwargs_mean=list(...), kwargs_covariance=list(...)) now fits an explicitly bounded native-R source-scientific FDApy 1.0.x UFPCA covariance-operator model from the ORIGINAL irregular observations.

It implements native pooled-time P-spline and local-polynomial mean smoothing, the source zero-penalty P-spline re-smoothing required to center data for covariance fitting, original-visit pairwise covariance, source-differenced measurement-noise estimation, PS/LP covariance smoothing with the source's distinct diagonal treatment, symmetric trapezoid-weighted covariance eigensystem, and conditional PACE scoring. The source-frozen public transform has a SEPARATE second centering operation: passing the source data to UFPCA.transform(method="PACE", method_smoothing="LP") smooths the trained mean with local-polynomial regression. The native R fit reproduces that distinct score-centering operation, then uses FDApy's internal pooled-grid linear interpolation, spectral-covariance pseudoinverse and inverse reconstruction.

Supplying source_fit_snapshot continues selecting the earlier independent conditional fixed-spectrum score stage, while calling without strict source mode preserves the historical explicit backend="fdapace" scientific alternative unchanged.

Native R reports matched mathematical source-estimand values and diagnostics but NOT a Python FDApy UFPCA backend instance. The source's numpy.linalg.eig order/sign convention and native R symmetric-eigen sorted principal-component convention are not bitwise equal. The reviewed raw-fitting domain is restricted to finite source-selected curves, normalize=FALSE, fit_smoothing="PS" or "LP", and source-supported score_smoothing="LP"; higher-order LP, unrestricted smoothing kwargs, covariance diagonal inclusion, Python objects/exceptions and complete numerical source certification remain unqualified.

See docs/native-fdapy-ufpca-ps-lp-source-20261112.md and inst/extdata/native_scoped_fdapy_submethod_gaps_20261112.csv.

Value

Each function returns its own documented native R, scientific-model, bridge, workflow or audit result; no single shared return type is asserted.
